correctness.rationale: A complete red-incidence-degree case split gives the exhaustive endpoint profiles (1,3),(2,2),(3,1) on red and (0,2),(1,1),(2,0) on blue. Connectedness isolates {1,3} or {0,2}, and unique monochromatic degree-three centres satisfy every closed-neighbourhood equation. Conversely each efficient code gives exactly two balanced assignments. Independent direct enumeration checks the original edge constraints, including all 70 labelled cubic graphs on six vertices. The power-of-two classification uses the explicitly cited Knor–Potočnik Theorem 1.2; three-colour Möbius upper bounds are explicit proper edge-colourings. Möbius enumeration uses the uniquely propagated code with a selected vertex, as in their Lemma 2.2.

value.rationale: A natural newly introduced graph colouring invariant is exactly classified in its two-colour regime on every connected simple cubic graph, including the full labelled colour-solution multiplicity. The rigidity theorem exposes the structural equivalence to perfect closed-neighbourhood codes and imports the nontrivial complete power-of-two vertex-transitive classification, distinguishing a Möbius obstruction family and giving its full exact colour count. This is not merely the previously established prism case or a re-enumeration of an old code table.
